before_times: What's wrong: it won't open or close, a loud bang, it's off its track, the opener, a remote, or a noise
Is a car stuck inside, and by when must it leave (this sets urgent)
How many doors, and single or double width
What the opener does: hums, clicks, or nothing
Is there a gap in a spring above the door: one, both, or can't tell
At the counter: which remote or opener, and its brand and model if known
after_time: Who will be there: an adult must be home for the whole visit (their name and mobile go on the secure page)
Are the cables at the bottom corners of the door still attached
About how old the opener is
The way into the garage, parking, and pets
Own or rent, and who pays: the customer, or the landlord or manager
secure_page_only: A photo of the spring area and the opener's label
The landlord's or manager's name and mobile
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the home's owner names may book for them.

stop.words: Someone hurt, or pinned under the door
stop.says: Call 911 now. Don't try to lift the door yourself.
stop.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

go_on.words: A loud bang, a broken spring, a snapped cable, or a door hanging crooked
go_on.says: Don't lift the door, pull the red release cord, or touch the springs. The door is very heavy now and can drop. Keep people, pets and the car clear.

go_on.words: An opener that won't stop, or won't go back up
go_on.says: Unplug the opener, and keep everyone clear of the door.
Don't force the door. A tech comes first; a ride is safer if you must leave sooner.

safety_and_stop_words.always: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

prep: Don't use the door or the opener if a spring or cable is broken
Clear the area under the door and around the opener
At the counter: bring the old remote, or the opener's model and a photo of its label; bring a board in an anti-static bag if you have one

skills: Doors off track, rollers and hinges
staff.supervision: A helper works only with a tech on the job, and never on springs alone.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit and same-day urgent jobs. A job sent now goes to the tech on call, then the backup set at sign-up. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
staff.stand_in: Another tech with the same skill, at the same window and price.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the home's owner names may book for them.

visit.done: The tech texts DONE with the bill's lines once the test passes, and photos after.
visit.changes_at_visit: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A new opener or a new door gets its own quote.
visit.before_work: Photos of the door, springs and opener before work.

license.need: Garage door work needs a license where the state, county or city licenses door or home repair contractors. Some places license it only above a job amount.
license.who: The company, where a license is required. Each door tech only where the state's form licenses door techs.
ask: The company's license number and class, where the state's form asks
Each door tech's own number, in their invite reply, only where the state asks
Insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one
license.insurance: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks: from the state form.
license.background: Only where the state's form asks.
